elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause opens: "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement or any Order Form for any reason, Vendor shall ..." — the obligations in (a)-(c) are triggered by every expiry and every termination, not only anticipated expiry.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: Limb (a): "at Customer's request, provide transition assistance for up to six months" — matches the six-month ceiling; the request condition tracks the model language and is not tied to expiry only.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (b): "within thirty days after that expiry or termination, return all Customer Data" — the clock is anchored to the termination/expiry event, not to a Customer request.

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: Limb (b): "return all Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format."

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: Limb (c): "after that return, delete Customer Data from its systems and certify the deletion to Customer in writing" — deletion is expressly sequenced after return.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Same inserted trigger language: "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement or any Order Form for any reason."

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: Six months of assistance in limb (a) exceeds the 90-day fallback floor.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (b) requires return of all Customer Data within thirty days after the expiry or termination.

reasons: The finding is correctly classified as missing: Section 10.1 references an "agreed transition period" without creating one, Section 10.2 addresses only Deliverables and refunds, and Section 16.5 expressly routes Customer Data away to Sections 11 and 15, which contain no export, return, or deletion-timing mechanic.
All six preferred elements are met in operative language, so the redline is position-complete at the preferred level (and a fortiori at the fallback).

Minimality holds: the proposal is a single concise insertion in the termination section with no deletions or paraphrase of surrounding text; it adds no survival tail, at-own-expense wording, cost allocation, or procedure beyond the checklist. Extending the trigger to "or any Order Form" is justified by the document's Order Form structure and Section 10.1's reference to "terminated subscription Services" (partial termination), so it is not surplus.

Intent is preserved: refund and Deliverables mechanics in 10.2, the access wind-down in 10.1, and the confidentiality return/destroy regime in 16.5 all survive without contradiction; the new clause supplies the substantive Customer Data exit mechanic that was absent.

Two housekeeping points for the drafter (not defects in the checklist): (i) the rendered insertion carries no section number although the rationale calls it Section 10.3 — number it so cross-references remain clean; (ii) Section 16.5's retained sentence "Customer Data remains governed by Sections 11 and 15" could be read as excluding the new Section 10 mechanic, and Section 11 is empty, so consider siting the clause in Section 15 or conforming the Section 16.5 cross-reference rather than adding a broad notwithstanding override.
